findings.claim: The breaker check (line 151) only runs at the top of the loop, before a candidate is started, so it can never observe two consecutive aborts that happen to be the last two candidates in the queue: the loop simply exhausts `candidates` and falls through to `ledger.close_batch(batch_id, "DRAINED")`. Concretely, with a two-candidate queue where both return `GATE_ERROR`/`PREFLIGHT_FAILED` (or any pairing of ABORT_STATES with nothing after), `consecutive_aborts` reaches 2 but no further iteration exists to evaluate the `>= _BREAKER_THRESHOLD` check at line 151, so the batch is closed and returned as `DRAINED` instead of `INFRASTRUCTURE`. This inverts the very distinction the module's own comments describe as the point of the breaker ("enough to tell 'the toolchain is broken' from 'three flaky tasks'") and is untested — every existing breaker test (e.g. `test_two_consecutive_aborts_fire_the_breaker`) supplies a third candidate so the check always gets one more iteration to fire on, masking the tail case.

`_attach_runs_minted_since` sweeps in every row from `runs` with `run_id > high_water AND batch_id IS NULL`, with no `repo_id` filter at all, and its own docstring (lines 62-70) justifies the lack of scoping solely on 'under K=1 nothing else can mint a run while one candidate's call is in flight' — but the ledger is a single WAL-mode SQLite file (`ledger.py:161-163`) meant to be shared across processes, and this module's own comments describe `saffron cell` and `replay.py` as real, expected sources of NULL-`batch_id` rows written concurrently with a batch. If either is invoked against this ledger (same repo or a different one) while a candidate's runner call is in flight and then raises, this sweep will attach that unrelated run — and its real billed spend — to tonight's batch, permanently rewriting `runs.batch_id` for a row this batch never produced. The tests only exercise a single in-process `Ledger` with a synchronous fake runner, so this cross-process race is invisible to the suite and true only in the fixture, not in production.

`_attach_runs_minted_since` is scoped to `run_id > high_water AND batch_id IS NULL` specifically so that pre-existing orphaned runs (left by `saffron/replay.py` and `saffron/cell/session.py`'s `create_run` calls outside a batch, both of which pass no `batch_id`) are never swept into tonight's batch when a runner raises mid-call. No test constructs such a pre-existing orphan before invoking `run_batch`: every test's ledger is freshly created and has zero rows before the crashing candidate mints its one run, so `_max_run_id` returning 0 in every test is indistinguishable from `_max_run_id` always returning 0. Replacing the query `"SELECT COALESCE(MAX(run_id), 0) AS m FROM runs"` with `"SELECT 0 AS m"` disables the high-water guard entirely (sweeping any and all `batch_id IS NULL` runs, including stray ones from `replay.py`) and every test in tests/test_batch.py still passes, silently reintroducing the exact spend-contamination bug the docstring says this scoping prevents.
